Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test case creates options with and without types set explicitly (Line 67 sets option "i" with type Number, line 68 option "f" without an explicit type). Then it parses arguments and calls getParsedOptionValue("f"). The test expects to get the string value "foo" back from the parsed option.

Inspecting CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue(String opt) (lines 113-124) reveals that the method fetches the option value string and then fetches the Option object. If either is null, it returns null. Otherwise, it calls TypeHandler.createValue(res, option.getType()). The key check is option.getType(). If option.getType() returns null, then the createValue method likely returns null or fails, explaining why getParsedOptionValue returns null for options without explicit type set.

The Option.getType() method (lines 186-189) just returns the type field, which is set through OptionBuilder.withType(Class). There is no fallback or default type set in Option or CommandLine.

The test uses OptionBuilder.hasArg().withType(Number.class) for option "i" but just OptionBuilder.hasArg() for "f". Since in the test getParsedOptionValue("f") returns null, this implies the Option.type for option "f" is null.

The current bug report summarizes this problem: getParsedOptionValue returns null unless Option.type is explicitly set. The user expects the default to be String. The root cause is that Option.type is null by default, causing TypeHandler.createValue to fail or return null.

No existing code sets a default type to String in Option or CommandLine. Hence, adding a default type to String either in the Option constructor or in CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue (e.g., treat null type as String.class) would fix the issue.

The recent bug report about Option constructors is unrelated.

Therefore, the failure occurs because the Option object's type is null by default when not explicitly set, leading getParsedOptionValue to return null instead of the expected String value.

Suggested fixes include initializing Option.type to String.class by default or handling null Option.type gracefully in getParsedOptionValue. Also, documenting this behavior is advised.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
